newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply down as gains evaporate.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply down as gains evaporate.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Thursday as late profit-taking swept the market despite several bullish factors, causing brokers to wonder if the index's recent bull run may have run out of steam.

The weighted index rocketed at the open on hopes that a decades-old ban on direct shipping between rivals Taiwan and China might finally end, peaking at 7,391.94 in early trade, but by the end of a wildly volatile session the index had reversed course and tumbled 71.22 points or 0.98 percent to 7,219.55.
Turnover was a heavy T$136.5 billion, the highest since April 15, 1996.

Prices opened higher on hopes that an unofficial consensus reached between negotiators from rivals Taiwan and Chinese on Wednesday in Hong Kong could enable direct shipping, prompting anticipation that the recent stock rally might continue.
Many asset-backed firms rose on separate news that Taiwan's finance ministry would allow businesses to reassess the values of assets bought before 1979, brokers said.

"The fact that profit-taking still occurred despite these bullish factors showed the market had hit a technical peak, and may have exhausted its upside room," said Michael Hung, senior analyst at Nikko Securities.
"Tomorrow (Friday) will be a key indicator of whether today's session was just a temporary setback, or the start of a downtrend," Hung added.
Before Thursday the market had gained more than 400 points in January in a sustained bull run that culminated with a six-year-high close on Wednesday.
Thursday's falls spread across the board, with electronics dropping 1.18 percent, financials losing 0.46 percent and plastics easing 1.11 percent.
A 7,150-7,250 range was seen for Friday.
